subject: Experiment charter: success definitions, eval method choice, and owners
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@healthly.com>; Sanjay Patel <sanjay@healthly.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Experiment charter: success definitions, eval method choice, and owners

Hi Elena / Sanjay —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight charter so we can move to a short, measurable pilot: 

TL;DR: Healthly runs a 3-week pilot (online shadow + offline eval) to validate intent detection and triage accuracy at 500 daily queries; success = 70%+ weighted F1 on clinical intents and <200ms 95th latency. Proposed owners: Logan (sales), Grace (success), Marissa (ops).

What Im proposing now (please confirm):
- Duration: 3 weeks active trial + 1 week buffer for data review
- Scope: 500 representative queries/day; two evaluation tracks (online shadow for latency and integration, offline scoring against annotated set for quality)
- Success metrics: weighted F1 >= 0.70 on clinical intents, false positive rate <= 15% for high-risk intents, 95th percentile latency < 200ms on Redwood Dedicated configuration
- Grading rubric: primary metric = weighted F1; secondary = latency and failure rate; well use a 3-tier pass/warn/fail threshold for each metric (spreadsheet attached)
- Owners & next steps: 
  - Logan (deal lead): coordinate contract and procurement checklist; target kick-off 2027-05-24
  - Grace (customer success): pilot runbook, data ingestion guidance, weekly syncs
  - Marissa (solutions/ops): test harness, shadow routing config, and evaluation scripts

Attachments: poc-success-criteria.xlsx (scoring rubric), redwood-poc-checklist.pdf (onboarding checklist)

Next steps: confirm scope and owners, share sample queries (anonymized) by EOD Friday, and well send a short MOU for the trial.

Thanks —
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: poc-success-criteria.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
Attachment: redwood-poc-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@healthly.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@healthly.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Experiment charter: success definitions, eval method choice, and owners

Logan — thanks for the summary. This aligns with internal expectations. A few clarifications before we lock dates:

1) Query volume: 500/day is fine for a representative slice, but can we phase up to 2k/day in week 3 if everything looks stable?
2) Annotated set: we can provide ~2,500 anonymized labeled examples within 4 business days; is that sufficient for the offline rubric?
3) Risk classes: for high-risk intents we want false positive <= 10% — can we make that a separate gating item?

Wed like an explicit fall-back plan if latency spikes during the shadow run (automatic traffic reroute to current rule engine). Also, please share the evaluation spreadsheet — looks like you attached it, but we couldn't open it on mobile.

Happy to proceed assuming those items are addressed. Sanjay and I are available for a 30-min kickoff Monday 2027-05-24 morning PST.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Product | Healthly.ai

Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Experiment charter: success definitions, eval method choice, and owners

Hi Elena / Sanjay —

Thanks for the quick reply and great questions. A few concrete notes from the ops side and a proposed evaluation choreography: 

1) Phased volume: yes — well start at 500/day (week 1), 1.5k/day (week 2), and 2k/day (week 3) if latency and error budgets allow. That will be controlled by a workload policy we push to the shadow runner.

2) Annotated set: 2,500 labeled examples is ideal. Well run k-fold holdouts and bootstrap confidence intervals for the weighted F1 and provide per-intent breakdowns. The offline eval will be the primary quality signal for release decisions.

3) High-risk gating: agreed — well treat the high-risk intents as a hard gate at <=10% false positives. If the gate fails, well mark the pilot as warn and discuss mitigations (threshold tuning, human-in-loop).

4) Latency fall-back: well provide an automated fallback route back to your rule engine with a 2-minute warmup window and a circuit-breaker at sustained 95th > 250ms for more than 5 minutes.

5) Deliverables & timeline: 
  - Today (20 May): Marissa to share test harness repo link and evaluation script snippets
  - 21 May: Healthly to share anonymized sample queries (1k) for initial smoke tests
  - 24 May (AM PST): Kickoff + access exchange (API keys, data upload link)
  - 24 May—14 Jun: Pilot run (3 weeks active)
  - 18 Jun: Post-pilot readout and gradebook

6) Ownership: Marissa = pilot ops and evaluation lead; Grace = customer success contact for schedule and user acceptance; Logan = contract and commercial path.

Ive attached a trimmed scoring rubric and the onboarding checklist. If youre ok, Ill open a shared Drive folder and grant you edit access to the rubric workbook so we can both adjust weights.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-poc-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)
